narrative: OMX30 enters Monday with conflicting signals: European peers rally on solid risk appetite while US equities stumble, creating a mixed-signal environment. The index sits in bull regime (+1.6% above 200-MA) but shows technical stress—MACD has crossed below signal line (hist= -8.438), RSI at 40 sits neutral without conviction, and ADX at 27.7 carries bearish directional bias. Rising US yields (4.988%, +71bp) support Swedish bank NIMs but compress tech multiples; the sharp oil decline (-5.86%) is defensive-positive for consumer purchasing power but signals demand concerns. USD/SEK strength (+0.43%) props exporters like Volvo and Atlas Copco. The index sits 4% from 52-week highs and -2.0% below the 50-MA—a range-bound setup vulnerable to mean reversion. Morning call: low-conviction rally attempt likely capped; watch for buyers at 3120 support.
morningBrief: OMX30 opens on uneven footing as Europe outperforms but US equity weakness and rising yields create headwinds. Technical picture is deteriorating: MACD below signal, ADX shows strong trend but with bearish undertone, and the index trading in lower half of Bollinger Bands suggests downside vulnerability despite +1.6% buffer above 200-MA. USD/SEK at 9.949 (+0.43%) is a tailwind for Volvo, Atlas Copco, and Ericsson, but the NASDAQ selloff (-0.21%) weighs on tech sentiment. Oil's -5.86% drop is a mixed bag—positive for consumer discretionary and manufacturing margins but signals global growth anxiety. Banks (18% weight) get a boost from higher yields but are not enough to offset broader uncertainty. Watch 3120 support on any dip; resistance remains at 3180 (50-MA). Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET could drive intraday volatility. Positioning: cautious long only with tight stops.
